figures.label: III
figures.caption: TABLE III. Normalized elastic moduli, normalized shear moduli, and Poisson's ratios of gyroid-based structural electrolyte microstructures with varying unit-cell scaling ratios (a:b:c) for various porosities ε. Small differences between symmetry-equivalent directions arise from STL geometry import and finite element meshing and are within the numerical precision of the simulations. Note: The effective shear moduli are obtained from the corresponding shear compliance terms. Effective shear moduli are normalized by the shear modulus of the solid phase Gs = Es/(2(1 + νs)). The effective Poisson's ratios are computed from the off diagonal compliance terms. Poisson's ratio νij denotes that the material is loaded along the i axis, and the contraction is measured along the j axis, and νijEj = νjiEi.

figures.caption: Eq. (1) — gyroid-like implicit isosurface: sin(2πx/a)cos(2πy/b) + sin(2πy/b)cos(2πz/c) + sin(2πz/c)cos(2πx/a) − t = 0 (a, b, c = scaling dimensions in x, y, z; t controls the volume fractions; a = b = c → conventional gyroid).
Eq. (12) — ionic current density i = −κl ∇ϕ (κl = κl I, isotropic liquid conductivity; ϕ = electrolyte potential).
Eq. (16) — macroscopic current density i_avg = (1/V_cell) ∫_Ωl i dV (integral over the liquid only, normalised by the WHOLE cell volume).
Eq. (17) — homogenized relation i_avg = −κ_eff (∇ϕ)_avg; reported conductivities = diagonal terms of κ_eff.
Eq. (18) — normalisation Ē_i = E_i^eff/E_s, κ̄_i = κ_i^eff/κ_l, i ∈ {x, y, z}.
Eq. (19) — tortuosity τ_i = ε (1/κ̄_i), i ∈ {x, y, z}; where ε is the porosity of the structural electrolytes.
